title: Super 30 Founder Anand Kumar Receives Special Achievement Award in Japan
excerpt: The Patna educator was honoured by CGC Group chairman Atsuhiro Horiuchi for Super 30's free IIT coaching and his Super Infinity initiative to take mathematics learning across borders.
body:
• Anand Kumar, founder of the Super 30 programme in Patna, has received a 'Special Achievement Award' in Japan for making quality education accessible to children from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
  • The award was presented by Atsuhiro Horiuchi, chairman and CEO of CGC Group, one of Japan's leading business groups.
  • The citation singled out Super 30, which has offered free coaching for IIT entrance examinations since 2002, and Super Infinity, Kumar's newer initiative to take mathematics learning across borders.
  • During the visit Kumar also reunited with Japanese technology leader Joi Ito, whom he had first met nearly 16 years ago.

Indian mathematician Anand Kumar, who founded the Super 30 programme that prepares talented students from poor families for India's IIT entrance examinations, has been honoured in Japan with a 'Special Achievement Award' for his contribution to education. The award was presented by Atsuhiro Horiuchi, chairman and CEO of CGC Group, according to India Today and an ANI report carried by Devdiscourse.

CGC Group is one of Japan's major business groups, with 202 member companies and 5,083 stores and annual business turnover exceeding 5.72 trillion yen, the ANI report said. The citation accompanying the award recognises Kumar for providing free, high-quality education to economically disadvantaged young people through Super 30, opening new possibilities in their lives.

"This honour does not belong to me alone. It belongs to all those children around the world who continue to struggle to fulfil their dreams despite difficult circumstances."

— Anand Kumar, founder of Super 30

From Super 30 to Super Infinity

Kumar started Super 30 in Patna in 2002, offering free coaching for IIT entrance examinations to talented students from underprivileged families. The citation made special mention of Super Infinity, his latest initiative, describing it as an effort to go beyond national borders and economic barriers and bring the joy of mathematics to children across the world. "From Super 30 to Super Infinity, my purpose has remained the same: no child should be deprived of a good education simply because of a lack of money," Kumar said after receiving the award.

Horiuchi expressed particular interest in Super Infinity's ongoing Japanese-language initiative, observing that children in Japan, too, would like to learn mathematics in more interesting and engaging ways beyond traditional classroom methods, according to the ANI report.

A reunion 16 years in the making

The Japan visit also brought a reunion with renowned Japanese technology entrepreneur and innovation leader Joi Ito, whom Kumar had first met nearly 16 years ago, Hungama reported. Kumar expressed his gratitude to Horiuchi and the CGC Group, saying the recognition would encourage him to continue working to make quality education accessible to more children.

For families in the diaspora who follow Super 30's story, the honour is a reminder of the programme's reach: a coaching initiative begun in Patna more than two decades ago is now being cited in Japan for a model — free, high-quality teaching for students who cannot pay — that its founder is attempting to extend internationally through Super Infinity.
